title: Temporal entity cleanup scratchpad
content:
Notes / goals:
- Create a minimal, consistent rule set for labeling temporal expressions (absolute dates, relative spans, recurring events) for the annotation team.
- Prioritize examples that break current model: mixed-format dates, sloppy user-entered text, partial dates (’Q1 2022’, ’spring 2019’), and timezone hints.

Quick heuristics (working):
1) If there is a full numeric date with clear separators and year (e.g., 03/05/2021, 2021-03-05), normalize to ISO (2021-03-05). If ambiguous mm/dd vs dd/mm and context is U.S. locale (user profile or dataset source), prefer mm/dd; otherwise flag for adjudication.
2) Partial dates: label as DATE and include normalized form when possible (’Q2 2020’ -> 2020-Q2; ’spring 2018’ -> 2018-SPRING). If uncertain, set normalized to UNKNOWN.
3) Relative phrases: translate to anchored spans only when an anchor exists in text (’three days ago’ relative to conversation timestamp). Otherwise label as RELATIVE_DATE with raw text preserved.
4) Timezones: annotate only when explicit (’PST’, ’UTC+2’, ’EST’). Don’t infer timezone from city names unless very explicit (’Jan 5 in Tokyo’ -> attach +09:00).
5) Ranges: label two tokens as a single DATE_RANGE if connected by hyphen, to, through. Normalize to start/end ISO where possible.

Edge cases and examples:
- "on 5/6" in dataset from UK news -> likely 6 May, but model currently assumes May 6. Flag 5/6 for review.
- "last Monday" in a multi-turn chat anchored to message t0. Store anchor id in metadata so QA can reproduce.
- "Q3-4 2019" -> ambiguous: is that Q3–Q4 (range) or malformed? Mark as DATE_RANGE with note.
- "2019-00-00" or ’2021-13-01’ -> tag as INVALID_DATE; do not normalize.

Labeler process notes:
- Use the "raw_text" label for anything we couldn’t normalize but still want the model to see.
- Add a free-text justification when choosing between dd/mm and mm/dd for ambiguous numerics. We need examples in adjudication queue.
- For datasets with timezone-sensitive tasks (scheduling, logs), create a separate pass to canonicalize to UTC and store original timezone token.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to surface locale reliably? For now: dataset source -> assume locale; otherwise mark ambiguous. TODO: add heuristics based on phone number country code and IP when available.
- Should we normalize natural language spans like "end of this month" to a range [YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD]? Pros: easier downstream; Cons: brittle if anchor missing. Proposal: normalize only when anchor timestamp present.
- Build a small unit test set (50 items) for the ingestion pipeline showing common failure modes. CX: ask Marco for 20 problematic customer examples (ticket DATA-4312).

QA checklist (for reviewers):
- Verify normalized form follows ISO or agreed shorthand (Qn, SPRING/FALL).
- Ensure relative dates include anchor id or are flagged.
- Confirm timezone tokens are preserved verbatim.
- Check that invalid dates are NOT coerced into plausible but wrong dates.

Quick sample annotations (labeler format: RAW -> LABEL -> NORMALIZED):
- "due 5/6" -> DATE -> 2024-05-06 (note: assumed mm/dd because dataset=us-customer-chat)
- "Q1 20" -> DATE -> 2020-Q1
- "three months ago" (anchor=msg-2345) -> RELATIVE_DATE -> anchor=2024-02-15
- "Aug 2018 - Nov 2018" -> DATE_RANGE -> 2018-08-01/2018-11-30

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. The heavier canonicalization/pipeline ops belong in label-tools PR (#88). Next steps:
- Draft a short one-pager for raters with 12 canonical examples. (Sofia)
- Sync with Marco and Aisha next Wed to triage ambiguous numeric dates.
- Push 50-item test set to GH repo and add CI check that flags invalid normalizations.

Slack refs: #data-ops, #labeler-questions. Confluence draft linked above is very rough; will move to shared_drives when we have something stable.

End of scratchpad.
